Do not filter, skip, or reinterpret.\n#\n# Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build` and compares every command's exit code and standard output\n# over the supplied data files with the known answer below. Statistic fields are empty when they do not apply.\ntype Column struct {\n\tName     string\n\tType     string\n\tRows     int\n\tNulls    int\n\tDistinct int\n\tMin      string\n\tMax      string\n\tSum      string\n\tMean     string\n\tMedian   string\n}\n\n// Describe profiles one column from its trimmed values.\nfunc Describe(name string, values []string) Column {\n\trows, nulls, distinct := Counts(values)\n\ttyp := typing.Infer(values)\n\tlo, hi := MinMax(typ, values)\n\tsum, mean, median := NumericStats(typ, values)\n\treturn Column{\n\t\tName: name, Type: typ,\n\t\tRows: rows, Nulls: nulls, Distinct: distinct,\n\t\tMin: lo, Max: hi, Sum: sum, Mean: mean, Median: median,\n\t}\n}\n\n// Counts returns the number of data values, the number of null values, and the number of\n// distinct non-null values. The values must already be trimmed; comparison is exact.\nfunc Counts(values []string) (rows, nulls, distinct int) {\n\tseen := make(map[string]struct{})\n\tfor _, v := range values {\n\t\tif reader.IsNull(v) {\n\t\t\tnulls++\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tseen[v] = struct{}{}\n\t}\n\treturn len(values), nulls, len(seen)\n}\n\n// MinMax returns the smallest and largest non-null value for a column of type typ.\n// Integers and numbers compare exactly; numbers are written with two decimal places.\n// Booleans report false/true in lowercase. Text and dates compare by byte value.\nfunc MinMax(typ string, values []string) (lo, hi string) {\n\tnonNull := nonNullValues(values)\n\tif len(nonNull) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\"\n\t}\n\tswitch typ {\n\tcase \"integer\", \"number\":\n\t\tlow, high := ratOf(nonNull[0]), ratOf(nonNull[0])\n\t\tfor _, v := range nonNull[1:] {\n\t\t\tr := ratOf(v)\n\t\t\tif r.Cmp(low) < 0 {\n\t\t\t\tlow = r\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif r.Cmp(high) > 0 {\n\t\t\t\thigh = r\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\tif typ == \"integer\" {\n\t\t\treturn low.Num().String(), high.Num().String()\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn fixed2(low), fixed2(high)\n\tcase \"date\", \"text\":\n\t\tlo, hi = nonNull[0], nonNull[0]\n\t\tfor _, v := range nonNull[1:] {\n\t\t\tif v < lo {\n\t\t\t\tlo = v\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif v > hi {\n\t\t\t\thi = v\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn lo, hi\n\tcase \"boolean\":\n\t\tlo, hi = \"true\", \"false\"\n\t\tfor _, v := range nonNull {\n\t\t\tif strings.EqualFold(v, \"false\") {\n\t\t\t\tlo = \"false\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tif strings.EqualFold(v, \"true\") {\n\t\t\t\thi = \"true\"\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn lo, hi\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\"\n\t}\n}\n\n// NumericStats returns the sum, mean, and median of an integer or number column. Every other\n// type returns three empty strings. Arithmetic is exact; rounding happens once when writing.\nfunc NumericStats(typ string, values []string) (sum, mean, median string) {\n\tif typ != \"integer\" && typ != \"number\" {\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\", \"\"\n\t}\n\tnonNull := nonNullValues(values)\n\tif len(nonNull) == 0 {\n\t\treturn \"\", \"\", \"\"\n\t}\n\tnums := make([]*big.Rat, len(nonNull))\n\ttotal := new(big.Rat)\n\tfor i, v := range nonNull {\n\t\tnums[i] = ratOf(v)\n\t\ttotal.Add(total, nums[i])\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(nums, func(i, j int) bool { return nums[i].Cmp(nums[j]) < 0 })\n\n\tn := len(nums)\n\tvar mid *big.Rat\n\tif n%2 == 1 {\n\t\tmid = nums[n/2]\n\t} else {\n\t\tmid = new(big.Rat).Add(nums[n/2-1], nums[n/2])\n\t\tmid.Quo(mid, big.NewRat(2, 1))\n\t}\n\tavg := new(big.Rat).Quo(total, big.NewRat(int64(n), 1))\n\n\tif typ == \"integer\" {\n\t\tsum = total.Num().String()\n\t} else {\n\t\tsum = fixed2(total)\n\t}\n\treturn sum, fixed2(avg), fixed2(mid)\n}\n\nfunc nonNullValues(values []string) []string {\n\tout := make([]string, 0, len(values))\n\tfor _, v := range values {\n\t\tif !reader.IsNull(v) {\n\t\t\tout = append(out, v)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn out\n}\n\n// ratOf parses a value already accepted by the integer or number pattern. Those patterns are\n// a subset of big.Rat syntax, so the parse cannot fail for a value that reached here.\nfunc ratOf(s string) *big.Rat {\n\tr, _ := new(big.Rat).SetString(s)\n\treturn r\n}\n\n// fixed2 writes x with exactly two decimal places, rounding once, half away from zero.\n// A negative result that rounds to zero is written without a sign.\nfunc fixed2(x *big.Rat) string {\n\ta := new(big.Rat).Abs(x)\n\t// floor(a*100 + 1/2) = floor((200*num + den) / (2*den)) for a non-negative a.\n\tnum := new(big.Int).Mul(a.Num(), big.NewInt(200))\n\tnum.Add(num, a.Denom())\n\tq := new(big.Int).Quo(num, new(big.Int).Mul(a.Denom(), big.NewInt(2)))\n\n\twhole, frac := new(big.Int).QuoRem(q, big.NewInt(100), new(big.Int))\n\ts := fmt.Sprintf(\"%s.%02d\", whole.String(), frac.Int64())\n\tif x.Sign() < 0 && q.Sign() != 0 {\n\t\ts = \"-\" + s\n\t}\n\treturn s\n}\nEOF\ncat > internal/freq/freq.go <<'EOF'\npackage freq\n\nimport (\n\t\"sort\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/reader\"\n)\n\n// Entry is one distinct non-null value and how many times it occurs.\ntype Entry struct {\n\tValue string\n\tCount int\n}\n\n// Top returns at most n of the most frequent non-null values. Values are trimmed before\n// counting. Entries are ordered by count descending, then value ascending by byte value.\nfunc Top(values []string, n int) []Entry {\n\tcounts := make(map[string]int)\n\tfor _, raw := range values {\n\t\tv := reader.Trim(raw)\n\t\tif reader.IsNull(v) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tcounts[v]++\n\t}\n\tentries := make([]Entry, 0, len(counts))\n\tfor v, c := range counts {\n\t\tentries = append(entries, Entry{Value: v, Count: c})\n\t}\n\tsort.Slice(entries, func(i, j int) bool {\n\t\tif entries[i].Count != entries[j].Count {\n\t\t\treturn entries[i].Count > entries[j].Count\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn entries[i].Value < entries[j].Value\n\t})\n\tif n < 0 {\n\t\tn = 0\n\t}\n\tif n < len(entries) {\n\t\tentries = entries[:n]\n\t}\n\treturn entries\n}\nEOF\ncat > internal/output/output.go <<'EOF'\npackage output\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/csv\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"strconv\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/freq\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/profile\"\n)\n\nvar (\n\tprofileHeader = []string{\"column\", \"type\", \"rows\", \"nulls\", \"distinct\", \"min\", \"max\", \"sum\", \"mean\", \"median\"}\n\tfreqHeader    = []string{\"value\", \"count\"}\n)\n\n// WriteProfile writes the profile header and one row per column as RFC 4180 CSV with LF endings.\nfunc WriteProfile(w io.Writer, cols []profile.Column) error {\n\tcw := csv.NewWriter(w)\n\tif err := cw.Write(profileHeader); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tfor _, c := range cols {\n\t\trec := []string{\n\t\t\tc.Name, c.Type,\n\t\t\tstrconv.Itoa(c.Rows), strconv.Itoa(c.Nulls), strconv.Itoa(c.Distinct),\n\t\t\tc.Min, c.Max, c.Sum, c.Mean, c.Median,\n\t\t}\n\t\tif err := cw.Write(rec); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tcw.Flush()\n\treturn cw.Error()\n}\n\n// WriteFreq writes the frequency header and one row per entry as RFC 4180 CSV with LF endings.\nfunc WriteFreq(w io.Writer, entries []freq.Entry) error {\n\tcw := csv.NewWriter(w)\n\tif err := cw.Write(freqHeader); err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\tfor _, e := range entries {\n\t\tif err := cw.Write([]string{e.Value, strconv.Itoa(e.Count)}); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn err\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tcw.Flush()\n\treturn cw.Error()\n}\nEOF\ngofmt -l . ; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMjqtH7N3cuMdocjQmRY","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016Y5VC7SrELQN8WN8HdENEX","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > internal/cli/cli.go <<'EOF'\n// Package cli implements the csvstat command line.\npackage cli\n\nimport (\n\t\"bytes\"\n\t\"encoding/csv\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"flag\"\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"io\"\n\t\"os\"\n\n\t\"csvstat/internal/freq\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/output\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/profile\"\n\t\"csvstat/internal/reader\"\n)\n\nconst (\n\texitOK       = 0\n\texitFailure  = 1 // the file cannot be opened or read\n\texitUsage    = 2 // the command line is malformed\n\texitRejected = 3 // the file was read but rejected, or a named column is absent\n\tdefaultTop   = 5\n)\n\nconst (\n\tprofileSynopsis = \"csvstat [--column <name>] <file>\"\n\tfreqSynopsis    = \"csvstat --freq <name> [--top <n>] <file>\"\n)\n\n// request is a parsed command line.\ntype request struct {\n\tfile      string\n\tcolumn    string\n\thasColumn bool\n\tfreqName  string\n\thasFreq   bool\n\ttop       int\n}\n\n// Run executes csvstat with the given arguments and returns the process exit code.\n// Standard output carries only profile or frequency CSV, and only on success.\n// Diagnostics go to stderr.\nfunc Run(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {\n\treq, ok := parseArgs(args, stderr)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn exitUsage\n\t}\n\n\tf, err := os.Open(req.file)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(stderr, \"csvstat: %v\\n\", err)\n\t\treturn exitFailure\n\t}\n\tdefer f.Close()\n\n\ttable, err := reader.Read(f)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tfmt.Fprintf(stderr, \"csvstat: %s: %v\\n\", req.file, err)\n\t\tvar parseErr *csv.ParseError\n\t\tif errors.As(err, &parseErr) {\n\t\t\treturn exitRejected\n\t\t}\n\t\treturn exitFailure\n\t}\n\n\ttable = reader.TrimTable(table)\n\tif err := reader.Validate(table); {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMjrvRs4G2igcxtA2Hus","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Aj9FkvjXeBpbqAcSuzJSMX","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cat > internal/reader/reader_test.go <<'EOF'\npackage reader\n\nimport (\n\t\"encoding/csv\"\n\t\"errors\"\n\t\"reflect\"\n\t\"strings\"\n\t\"testing\"\n)\n\nfunc mustRead(t *testing.T, in string) Table {\n\tt.Helper()\n\ttbl, err := Read(strings.NewReader(in))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read(%q) error: %v\", in, err)\n\t}\n\treturn tbl\n}\n\nfunc TestReadHeaderThenRows(t *testing.T) {\n\ttbl := mustRead(t, \"a,b\\n1,2\\n3,4\\n\")\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(tbl.Header, []string{\"a\", \"b\"}) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Header = %q\", tbl.Header)\n\t}\n\twant := [][]string{{\"1\", \"2\"}, {\"3\", \"4\"}}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(tbl.Rows, want) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Rows = %q, want %q\", tbl.Rows, want)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadQuotedComma(t *testing.T) {\n\ttbl := mustRead(t, \"note\\n\\\"remote, part-time\\\"\\n\")\n\tif len(tbl.Rows) != 1 || len(tbl.Rows[0]) != 1 || tbl.Rows[0][0] != \"remote, part-time\" {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Rows = %q, want one value %q\", tbl.Rows, \"remote, part-time\")\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadInvalidUTF8NotRejected(t *testing.T) {\n\t_, err := Read(strings.NewReader(\"a\\n\\xff\\xfe\\n\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Read returned error %v for invalid UTF-8, want nil\", err)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadRaggedRecordReturned(t *testing.T) {\n\ttbl, err := Read(strings.NewReader(\"a,b\\n1,2,3\\n\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read error: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif len(tbl.Rows) != 1 || !reflect.DeepEqual(tbl.Rows[0], []string{\"1\", \"2\", \"3\"}) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Rows = %q, want the extra-field record unchanged\", tbl.Rows)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadLineNumbers(t *testing.T) {\n\ttbl := mustRead(t, \"a,b\\n1,\\\"two\\nlines\\\"\\n3,4\\n\")\n\twant := []int{2, 4}\n\tif !reflect.DeepEqual(tbl.Lines, want) {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Lines = %v, want %v\", tbl.Lines, want)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadEmptyInput(t *testing.T) {\n\ttbl, err := Read(strings.NewReader(\"\"))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tt.Fatalf(\"Read error: %v\", err)\n\t}\n\tif tbl.Header != nil || len(tbl.Rows) != 0 || len(tbl.Lines) != 0 {\n\t\tt.Errorf(\"Read(empty) = %+v, want zero Table\", tbl)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunc TestReadHeaderOnlyHasNoRows(t Standard library only.\n- Reader: `encoding/csv` with `FieldsPerRecord = -1`, line numbers from `FieldPos`, `TrimTable`, `IsNull`, and `Validate` (empty file, empty or repeated header, ragged record with line number).\n- Typing, profile, and frequencies: integer, number, date (calendar-validated), boolean, text, and empty, with exact `math/big` min, max, sum, mean, and median. Numbers round once, half away from zero, to two places. Frequencies sort by count, then byte value.\n- CLI: a local `FlagSet`, usage errors with exit 2 and both synopses, exit 1 for unreadable files, exit 3 for rejected content or an absent column, and output buffered so nothing reaches stdout on failure.\n- Tests: about 150 Go tests, including the names the specs require. The block-1 test in `cli_test.go` expected `a.csv` to exit 0.
